chunks: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about ruku' and sujud: have they been revealed in the Qur'an? He said: Yes.
The saying of Allah, the Exalted: “O you who have faith, bow and prostrate.”
So I said: What is the limit of ruku' and sujud? He said: As for what suffices you in ruku', it is three tasbihat: you say, “Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah,” three times.

key_terms.ارْكَعُوا: bow; a Qur'anic command establishing ruku'
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an as the revealed source cited for the ruling
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَاتٍ: utterances of glorification of Allah recited in worship
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to Allah; the formula of tasbih recited in ruku'
key_terms.وَاسْجُدُوا: prostrate; a Qur'anic command establishing sujud

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tasbih that suffices in ruku' according to a hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ruku' and sujud are established in the Qur'an through the divine command to bow and prostrate. It also gives a legal minimum for dhikr in ruku', namely three tasbihat saying “Subhan Allah” three times.
